subject: dinner plate at night
title: What If You Always Ate Dinner Late at Night?

scenes.text: What if you always ate dinner late at night? Same food, same calories, different body.
Harvard scientists fed volunteers identical meals, just four hours later in the day.
Within days, the hunger hormone rose against the fullness hormone by about a third.
Their bodies also burned about five percent fewer calories while awake. Same plate, slower engine.
Even their fat tissue switched genes toward storing fat instead of burning it.
So the clock matters, not just the plate. Your body handles the same meal differently after dark.

description:
In a 2022 Cell Metabolism study from Brigham and Women's Hospital, 16 volunteers ate identical meals on an early schedule and on a schedule shifted four hours later.
Late eating raised hunger, increased the ghrelin-to-leptin ratio by about 34%, cut waking energy expenditure by about 5% and shifted fat-tissue genes toward fat storage.
